items.title: AI trader / linear family: is a multinomial logit as good as LightGBM on the BTC/ETH/SOL 15m volatility-regime heads? (family has 0 registered models)
items.summary: On the SAME 15m v002 shards, features, purged folds and final-90-day holdout, does a plain numpy multinomial logistic regression (linear_logit family, 0 registered models) come within 0.01 macro-F1 of the incumbent LightGBM regime learner on ALL of BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT and SOLUSDT? If so the regime axis does not need a boosted tree, and a zero-dependency, interpretable head is a live option.
items.whyItMatters: ml_plan_status.py --diversity (2026-10-13): linear_logit has 0 registered models and 0 open plan items; gbdt is 75 of 96 (78%). All three advisory heads are GBDT. Nobody has measured how much of the head's macro-F1 is the tree and how much is just the rolling-vol feature. DATASET PATHS UNVERIFIED FROM THIS SANDBOX: the trainer shards are not reachable here. The 15m v002 BTC/ETH/SOL shards and the base feature names are the ones queued unit RQ-20261012-75b2-19..21 already declare (MEASURED present on the trainer 2026-10-11 per RQ-20261011-9da8-01); a missing column lands as a dead NaN feature or producer_failed, which research-ops must read as a ROUTE FAULT (fix the path, re-queue), never as a verdict.

rule.statistic: Paired per-fold macro-F1 difference (logit minus LightGBM) on identical purged expanding walk-forward folds (5 folds, embargo 96 rows, min_train_frac 0.4) and on the holdout window, per symbol; mean over folds. Applied by ml_bakeoff.py evaluate_rule from this unit's ml_bakeoff.rule.
rule.text: PASS (non-inferior) IF logit - lgbm macro-F1 >= -0.010 on the CV mean on ALL THREE symbols AND >= -0.010 on the holdout on all three: a linear head is a registrable alternative family. FAIL IF logit - lgbm < -0.030 on the CV mean on EVERY symbol (the tree is doing real work everywhere; closes only this untuned unweighted logit on these 6 features). INDETERMINATE otherwise (mixed by symbol), or if folds < 3 or an arm is unavailable.

items.title: Session/time-of-day, trend_donchian_eth_4h: does skipping one pre-registered UTC session block (Asia 00-07, US-open 12-16, late 20-23) beat the declared entry net of the full cost stack?
items.summary: M21 round 3 mined only two shared hour pockets (4h donchian hour 0, the 19-20 UTC pocket) and recorded time_of_day = n/a for the 1h/2h families: per-leg hour cells were deliberately NOT mined. This unit does not mine either. It tests three session blocks fixed BEFORE any run for market-structure reasons (Asia low-liquidity, US cash-open volatility, late-US/roll), applied identically to trend_donchian_eth_4h (ETHUSDT 4h). On the pinned 730d window (2024-10-05 .. 2026-10-04 23:59), same cost stack as the evidence builder, does skipping any one block (signal-bar open hour, UTC) beat the declared entry by a material margin, with no worse drawdown and in at least 3 of 4 calendar folds?
items.whyItMatters: Session structure is a cross-asset claim, not a per-leg one: the same three blocks are run on seven crypto legs in seven sibling units (RQ-20261013-407c-10..15 and -19) so a real session effect must reproduce across legs and timeframes, while a lone pass is read as noise. Fees, funding and liquidity all vary by session; if one block is consistently the drag it is a portfolio-wide entry filter, the cheapest structural lever there is.

Arms: B = leg as declared, SA = --skip-hours=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7, SU = --skip-hours=12,13,14,15,16, SL…
rule.text: indeterminate IF the positive control fails or n(B) < 39 (underpowered: no verdict, extend the window or redesign; never FAIL on thin n). A candidate C PASSES iff dR >= 1.5 R AND dDD <= 0 AND fold_wins >= 3 of 4. PASS IF any candidate passes (best = highest dR; the script's generic label reads 'reachable_lever_beats_removed'): a Tier-3 PROPOSAL note on the owning checklist row for the manager, never a config edit; two passing candidates within 0.5 R of each other is a preference, not a finding. FAIL IF none passes (script label 'no_reachable_lever_beats_removed'): the declared skip-hours stands; the axis is recorded honest_negative on this window. The 1.5 R bar, the drawdown clause, the 3-of-4 fold majority and the 39 floor are not changed after any result.

items.title: AI trader / probability quality: do the 15m regime learners beat the class prior on LOG-LOSS, not only on thresholded macro-F1? (the prerequisite for conformal abstention)
items.summary: On the 15m v002 shards (BTC/ETH/SOL), purged CV and holdout, does LightGBM or a numpy logit beat the class-prior probability on LOG-LOSS by at least 0.005 nats on all three symbols? Macro-F1 is an operating-point metric and the volatile label has a ~4.6% base rate (the base-rate cliff, ROADMAP T0.1); log-loss grades the probabilities themselves.
items.whyItMatters: Conformal abstention (RQ-20261011-9da8-03, blocked) and any confidence-gated use of a regime head need calibrated, better-than-prior probabilities. Every queued ML unit grades macro-F1; none grades probability quality. A head that wins on F1 but not on log-loss is selecting a threshold, not carrying information, and the conformal lever would be built on sand. DATASET PATHS UNVERIFIED FROM THIS SANDBOX: the trainer shards are not reachable here. The 15m v002 BTC/ETH/SOL shards and the base feature names are the ones queued unit RQ-20261012-75b2-19..21 already declare (MEASURED present on the trainer 2026-10-11 per RQ-20261011-9da8-01); a missing column lands as a dead NaN feature or producer_failed, which research-ops must read as a ROUTE FAULT (fix the path, re-queue), never as a verdict.

rule.statistic: Paired per-fold difference in multiclass log-loss (prior minus learner, signed so positive = learner better) on identical purged folds (5, embargo 96) and on the holdout, per symbol; mean over folds. ml_bakeoff.py evaluate_rule applies ml_bakeoff.rule.
rule.text: PASS IF a candidate (lgbm or logit) beats the class prior by >= +0.005 nats on the CV mean on ALL THREE symbols AND by >= 0 on the holdout on all three: the head carries probabilistic information, and the conformal lever is worth building. FAIL IF no candidate beats the prior by >= 0 on the CV mean on ANY symbol (macro-F1 skill is a threshold artifact; the conformal lever is not worth building on these heads at this feature set). INDETERMINATE otherwise, or if folds < 3 or an arm is unavailable. headline_checks reports lgbm minus logit on log-loss.
